I follow Harmful Opinions and very much appreciate the videos he's made. However, I think people are taking much more out of what he's saying - particularly the speculation - than he is actually saying. He is advocating that people judge for themselves if they are okay with using Candid given what is made known and what is unknown.

I don't think that Bindu is lying, per say, but I think she is completely working against the company though her actions, and I think she is a bit deluded. This is especially the case when she is talking about the future of the AI; my thoughts are in line with the points raised in the first video. And on top of the company being sold, investors (the people who are funding the ads, presumably) can have a lot of weight on the actions of a company and so far there has not been made available a legally binding statement regarding future sale of the AI and derived technology.

I think it was absolutely fucking retarded that any skeptic has agreed to anything that disallows them criticism for two fucking years. A lot can happen in that time, and there is so much already to criticize. I think there is some merit in the idea that so many people who might be critical of the platform have been approached for these NDAs, as outlined by the first video. I also think that the people who have sponsored Candid should have talked about it with their subscribers before taking the money.

Ultimately, though, my decision lies with the technology, and not the company or the app. I think the idea of the app is sound and the execution, as explained to us, is terrible. However, language processing AIs are complicated. Even the people who make them don't necessarily fully understand the nuance of it. They are, by their design, a black box. No one should expect it to be perfect. I don't think it's right of them to look to sources of discourse outside the app, and I think they needed to make a much stronger effort to get people of all different spheres - bloggers, gamers, etc.

All that said, I want to be clear that I will not support use of app. Largely, this is because of the company. My opinion, as I said in my comment, is torn about the app. I never said that I was torn as to whether or not I would use it. In the future if the company can demonstrate that the AI is neutral - that it did not develop incidental bias - then I would be more open to using the app. I am a fan of emerging technology, and language processing is a fascinating area in AI. Of course, with each new social technology comes new concerns about it's use, but that's a different issue entirely.
